entities.name: Louis the Stammerer
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Louis II the Stammerer (Louis le Bègue; 846–879) was King of Aquitaine and, after Charles the Bald’s death, King of West Francia for a brief reign (877–879). Physically frail and politically constrained, he inherited a Carolingian West Francia already strained by Viking pressure and aristocratic autonomy.

His short rule and the succession of his sons Louis III and Carloman II accelerated the fragmentation of Charles the Bald’s realm. Contemporary stigma around his speech defect entered his enduring epithet.

Louis the Stammerer marks the thinning of late Carolingian royal authority in West Francia.
